channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Paramount settles with US states to clear Warner Bros. mega-merger
item.description: Paramount has reached a settlement with a group of US states that clears the way for its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, officials announced Monday, creating a Hollywood empire spanning television, news and cinema.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Paramount settles with US states, clearing path for Warner Bros. merger
item.description: Paramount has reached a settlement with California and 11 other states that clears a major legal hurdle to its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, with the deal imposing commitments on film production, jobs and editorial independence at CNN and CBS News.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Ethiopia's main armed groups form anti-government alliance
item.description: In tonight's edition, a coalition of opposition groups band together in the hope of ousting Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Also, I speak to the deputy chief of the UN's peacekeeping mission in DR Congo. And with just a few days to go before the legislative elections, young Moroccans are torn between hope and skepticism ahead of the crucial vote.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: Paramount, US states settle antitrust lawsuit over Warner Bros. acquisition
item.description: Paramount Skydance has settled a lawsuit with a dozen US states that sought to block its acquisition of Warner Brothers, as well as with the Writers Guild of America. California's Attorney General said that while the settlement addressed concerns over competition and protection, it did not mean a vote of support for the deal.
item.dc:creator: Yuka ROYER

item.title: Ed Sheeran hit by viral false claims after Macklemore controversy
item.description: Ed Sheeran’s controversial US tour has sparked a wave of viral rumours. A false claim that his music was removed from Spotify racked up more than 3 million views on X, despite his his music remaining available. Another video, viewed over 14 million times, falsely suggested Sheeran was now defiantly performing solo after all his support acts withdrew, but not only is the footage dated, but Sheeran has indeed replaced the backing musicians. Vedika Bahl fact-checks in Truth or Fake.
item.dc:creator: Vedika BAHL

item.title: Forbidden Stories on Trump deportation system: FRANCE 24's 'Ice, Trump and Africa'
item.description: Sofia Alvarez Jurado, investigative journalist, member of the Deportation project speaks about the international investigation into Trump’s migrant policy.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Infantino says open to FIFA reform talks after World Cup controversy
item.description: FIFA ⁠President Gianni Infantino on Monday proposed an external review of how the football association makes decisions, including who has a say in major initiatives. Infantino ​faced backlash and calls for a boycott over the summer after proposing to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: France's new coach Zinedine Zidane leads first training session
item.description: France coach Zinedine Zidane on Monday oversaw his first training session with Les Bleus ahead of the new Nations League campaign. The 1998 World Cup winner led a dozen of his players through a light training session under the gaze of some 50 journalists.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 'Banking on a national brand': Bolsonaro sons Carlos, Jair Renan run for power in Brazil's south
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro is not the only member of his family campaigning in his father’s shadow. The former president's eldest son, who is now polling neck and neck with incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, can count on two of his brothers, who are standing in the senatorial and legislative elections. In Santa Catarina, one of Brazil’s most pro-Bolsonaro southern states, their surname alone is enough to secure victory.
item.dc:creator: Fanny LOTHAIRE

item.title: ‘National security threat’: Trump’s latest attack on US media
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday accused mainstream media outlets of being a “cancer” and national security threat in his latest attack on members of the press. It comes after Trump barred journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, with the three media outlets saying Monday they would sue the Trump administration, calling the ban a “blatant violation” of the First Amendment.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Typhoon Dujuan: Japan urges two million to evacuate
item.description: Japan’s Meteorological Agency has warned of an "imminent threat to life" as Typhoon Dujuan bears down on the country, with nearly two million people urged to evacuate across six prefectures, including Tokyo.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: French singer Amanda Lear accuses US star Miley Cyrus of 'copying' 1970s hit
item.description: French disco diva Amanda Lear accused Miley Cyrus on Monday of plagiarising her 1970s song "The Sphinx" in the US pop star's new track, "Redlights". However, Lear later added that she was not interested in a lawsuit.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Bayeux Tapestry craze prompts photo ban at British Museum
item.description: The British Museum said on Monday that it has banned people from taking photos of the Bayeux Tapestry to prevent crowds from backing up at the new exhibit. The 1,000-year-old artwork is on display in the UK after an unprecedented loan from France, and tickets are sold out until December 31.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: EU fines Google €403 million for improperly using location data
item.description: Ireland, on behalf of the European Union, said Monday it had fined Google €403 million for improperly using users' location data between May 2018 and February 2020. However, the eight-year delay drew some criticism, as the European Consumer Organisation said that "can be as harmful as no enforcement at all".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Merz’s election setback: What it means for Germany?
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and CDU representatives held a press conference on Monday, September 21, after the party suffered its worst regional election defeat in postwar Germany. Merz called the result in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania a “disaster”, as the CDU fell below the 5% threshold for entering the state parliament. Helmut Schmidt fellow at the German Marshall Fund of the US, Markus Ziener, shares further details.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France and Canada deepen economic and defense ties
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney have announced plans to deepen economic ties between their countries following a meeting at the weekend. Macron welcomed Carney in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, a French territory off the coast of Canada’s Newfoundland. The two leaders discussed opportunities to share infrastructure in the space and defence sectors, as Canada’s trade relationship with the US deteriorates and Europe looks to diversify its energy supplies. Bryan Quinn has more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Saudi Arabia left without US help against Houthis
item.description: Saudi Arabia is weighing Washington’s refusal to help fend off Houthi attacks after Riyadh requested US assistance, despite the two countries being longstanding allies and President Donald Trump and his family maintaining close personal ties with Saudi leaders. France 24 International affairs commentator Douglas Herbert shares further details on this alliance.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: UK: Fallout over Charles Spencer’s Diana Memoir
item.description: In the UK, fallout continues over the explosive memoirs of Princess Diana’s brother. Charles Spencer on Sunday accused King Charles of “gaslighting” him over his account of events surrounding Diana’s death, detailed in a book due to be released on Tuesday. Earl Spencer claims the monarch was “giddily elated” in the immediate aftermath of her death. Carys Garland has the story.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Government hosts energy meeting amid fuel price tensions
item.description: The French government is holding urgent meetings today as it looks for ways to tackle rapidly rising fuel prices. Drivers are paying record-high prices for diesel, as the war in Iran disrupts crude oil shipments from the Middle East. But with public discontent growing, the government has limited options, as France’s finances are already under pressure. This report is from Bryan Quinn and our colleagues at France Télévisions.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: French farmers turn to tropical crops amid rising temperatures
item.description: In the south of France, climate change is reshaping the region’s fruit production. Rather than fighting against it, a growing number of farmers are learning how to work with it – turning to tropical crops, now well-suited to the local climate. Bananas, papaya and even dragon fruit are being grown in greenhouses but also in open fields, without heating or pesticides. Our Down to Earth team reports.
item.dc:creator: Valérie DEKIMPE

item.title: Pope Leo heads to France amid church scandals
item.description: Preparations are underway in France for Pope Leo’s visit from September 25 to 28. During his trip, the Pontiff is expected to meet victims of church sexual abuse, as the Catholic Church faces renewed scrutiny following recent scandals. Delano D'Souza reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Music show: Meet Ed Banger Records' new girl Tatyana Jane and wild Jazz band Buck
item.description: This week on Arts24, music editor Marjorie Hache chats to Buck's saxophonist. He tells us more about how the six-piece came together during lockdown and took their name from the antler-sporting animal to make psychedelic wild jazz. They are currently touring their new album "Animal Boisé". We also meet French Cameroonian Dj Producer Tatyana Jane, Ed Banger Records' first female signing in two decades. Plus, we take a look at new releases by Leon Bridges and M83.
item.dc:creator: Marjorie HACHE

item.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico to sue Trump administration after White House ban
item.description: US media outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico announced Monday they were filing suit after US President Donald Trump banned their journalists from the White House last week. The ban on the three outlets marks an escalation in the Trump administration's years-long assault on the country's press freedoms.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Two tankers hit by 'unknown projectile' or debris in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday by either an "unknown projectile" or debris, a maritime security agency said. United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations added that at least two crew members were injured in the first incident, and both vessels will continue to their next port of call.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
